content: 1. Moderate CYP2C8 inducers reduce the plasma concentrations of tucatinib, potentially diminishing its therapeutic efficacy. 2. Rifampin decreases the levels of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism, rendering coadministration contraindicated. 3. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 4. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ulipristal by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 6. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use is not recommended; consider alternative therapies. 7. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of vardenafil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 9. Rifampin reduces the levels of vemurafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers; consider alternative treatments with less CYP3A induction. 11. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of verapamil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 13. Rifampin reduces the levels of vorapaxar by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 15. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Avoid using voxilaprevir and rifampin together. 16. Rifampin is contraindicated when coadministered with the combination of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir, as per prescribing information. 17. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 18. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of intranasal zavegepant through mechanisms involving OATP1B3 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 19. OATP1B3 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to zavegepant, an OATP1B3 substrate. 20. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of zuranolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Rifampin decreases the levels of abiraterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase abiraterone dosage frequency from once daily to twice daily. 22. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of alfentanil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of alosetron by inducing both CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of rifampin by reducing its absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 26. Magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of rifampin by decreasing its absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 27. Magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of rifampin by reducing its absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 28. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ambrisentan by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of amikacin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inducing CYP2C19, CYP3A4 metabolism, and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Rifampin reduces the levels of amobarbital by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of antipyrine by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of rifampin by increasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Apalutamide weakly induces OATP1B1, potentially decreasing systemic exposure to OATP1B1 substrates. 36. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of armodafinil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of artesunate by increasing its metabolism. Monitor for reduced efficacy due to decreased AUC and peak plasma concentration of the active metabolite (DHA). 38. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of asenapine by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of atogepant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of atogepant through OATP1B1 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 41. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Rifampin decreases the levels of atovaquone by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of avanafil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients with erectile dysfunction for reduced effectiveness. 44. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of avatrombopag by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 45. When treating ITP, coadministration of avatrombopag with moderate or strong dual CYP2C9/3A4 inducers requires an increased starting dose of avatrombopag. Refer to the drug monograph for specific recommendations. 46. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of rifampin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of belumosudil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg PO BID when coadministered with strong CYP3A inducers. 49. Rifampin reduces the levels of bendamustine by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers coadministered with benzhydrocodone, as plasma hydrocodone concentrations may increase, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 51. Rifampin decreases the levels of berotralstat by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Conversely, berotralstat increases the levels or effects of rifampin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Monitor or titrate P-gp substrate doses if coadministered. 52. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of bexagliflozin by inducing UGT1A9 metabolism. If coadministered with a UGT1A9 inducer, consider adding another antihyperglycemic agent for additional glycemic control. 53. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of bortezomib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of bosentan by inducing CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Bosutinib increases the levels of rifampin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Rifampin reduces the levels of brentuximab vedotin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Double the brexpiprazole dose over 1–2 weeks if coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. 59. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of brivaracetam by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Increase the brivaracetam dose up to 100% (i.e., double the dosage) in patients receiving concomitant rifampin treatment. 60. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of budesonide by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of buprenorphine buccal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for withdrawal symptoms. Implant removal may be necessary if the CYP3A4 inducer cannot be discontinued. 65. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of buprenorphine transdermal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider increasing the transdermal dosage until stable. Monitor for withdrawal symptoms. 66. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels to ensure adequacy. Transition to an adjustable formulation if necessary. 67. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of bupropion by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Rifampin decreases the levels of butabarbital by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Rifampin reduces the levels of butalbital by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 71. Rifampin reduces the half-life of calcifediol by stimulating microsomal hydroxylation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 72. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of calcitriol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 73. Calcium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of rifampin by decreasing its absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 74. Calcium/vitamin D reduces the levels or effects of rifampin by decreasing its absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 75. Rifampin decreases the levels of canagliflozin by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 76. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
